subject: Our World and Our People
name: KG2 Our World and Our People
description: The KG2 curriculum deepens learners' understanding of themselves, their families, and the wider world through integrated thematic strands, emphasizing inquiry, creativity, and practical skills.

strands.title: ALL ABOUT ME
strands.description: Learners explore their identity, body parts and functions, personal hygiene, healthy living, environmental health, and personal safety.

subStrands.title: I am a wonderful and unique creation
subStrands.description: Learners describe themselves positively and appreciate the unique features that make each person special.

contentStandards.description: Children in a circle, taking turns holding a 'talking ball'. One child is speaking confidently about what makes them special. The teacher listens with a smile. A poster on the wall says 'I am Special'.

indicators.description: A semi-circle arrangement in a classroom. Learners are passing a colorful ball. The child with the ball is standing and gesturing to their chest, describing themselves. Others are listening.

exemplars.description: A child holding a ball in a classroom circle, smiling and pointing to their face. The teacher encourages them to use positive words. The setting is a bright, airy Ghanaian classroom.

indicators.description: A teacher holding a storybook, pointing to the front cover. She gestures to her own front/chest to make a comparison between the 'front of the book' and 'front of the body'. Children observe keenly.

exemplars.description: Close-up of a teacher explaining the back cover of a book to students sitting on a mat. She turns the book over. The children touch their own backs to make the connection.

indicators.description: Shared reading session. A large Big Book is open on an easel. Children are looking at the pictures and discussing the characters. One child raises a hand to say something positive about the character.

exemplars.description: Children dramatizing a story from a Big Book. One child acts as the 'unique' character, standing proudly. Others clap. The teacher holds the book open to the relevant scene.

indicators.description: A name-matching game. Children are holding name cards. They are looking for a friend who has a matching name card or the same starting letter. They look excited to find their match.

exemplars.description: A child running towards the teacher with a name tag, matching it to one the teacher is holding. Other children are checking their tags. A fun, active literacy game.

indicators.description: Teacher writing a large letter on the chalkboard. Children are writing the same letter in the air with their fingers. Some are tracing it on their desks. Focus is on letter formation.

exemplars.description: Children writing a letter and a keyword (e.g., 'Face') in their exercise books. They are using pencils and sitting at wooden desks. The teacher walks around checking their work.

indicators.description: Children drawing in their sketchbooks. One child is drawing a hand, another a leg. They are using crayons. They label their drawings with simple text.

exemplars.description: A pair of learners showing each other their drawings of body parts. One points to a drawing of an eye and explains why they like it. Collaborative learning.

indicators.description: Numeracy lesson. Children are counting sets of body parts (e.g., 2 eyes, 10 fingers) on a poster. They are holding up number cards to match the quantity.

exemplars.description: Pairs of learners checking body parts. One counts the other's fingers. They place counters on a table to represent the number 10. Practical math.
Children grouped in fives. They are counting the total number of hands in their group. They are laughing and raising their hands.

subStrands.title: The parts of the human body and their functions
subStrands.description: Learners identify external and internal body parts and describe what they do.

contentStandards.description: Children placing their hands on their chests to feel their heartbeats. They look surprised and focused. A teacher explains the heart's function using a diagram.

indicators.description: Group activity. Children running around the block and then stopping to feel their heartbeat. They are talking about the 'thump-thump' feeling.

exemplars.description: Children pointing to the location of the brain (head) and stomach (belly) on their own bodies. A poster nearby shows these internal organs.

indicators.description: Teacher using a KWL chart on the board. She writes what children 'Know' about the stomach. Children are raising hands to suggest ideas like 'it holds food'.

exemplars.description: Read-aloud session about the body. The teacher reads an informational text. Children share what they have 'Learned' (L) about the brain helping them think.

indicators.description: Children constructing simple sentences orally. One child pretends to eat and rubs their stomach, saying 'My stomach digests food'. Peer learning.

exemplars.description: A child holding a picture card of a heart. They say a sentence about it. Other children clap. Vocabulary application.

indicators.description: Teacher modeling writing the letter 'S' (for Stomach) on the board. Children write it on the back of the friend sitting in front of them. Fun writing practice.

exemplars.description: Children writing 'Brain' and 'Heart' in their exercise books. They carefully follow the red and blue lines. They look focused.

indicators.description: Children performing 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' with high energy. They touch each part as they sing. The teacher leads the action.

exemplars.description: A music session where children sing a local song identifying body parts. They dance and point rhythmically. Joyful atmosphere.

indicators.description: Children sitting at desks drawing a full-body self-portrait. They label parts like 'head', 'leg' using invented spelling. They share with a partner.

exemplars.description: A child showing their drawing. They have written 'My Heart' next to the chest area. They explain it to a friend.

indicators.description: Children comparing piles of bottle tops. One pile has 15, another has 5. They use cards with symbols '>' and '<' to show which is greater.

exemplars.description: Math lesson. Children ordering number cards from 1 to 20 on the floor. They place corresponding numbers of stones next to the cards.

subStrands.title: Personal hygiene and caring for the parts of the body
subStrands.description: Learners discuss and practise personal hygiene and proper care of the body.

contentStandards.description: Children demonstrating care for the body. One simulates cutting nails with a toy clipper. Another combs hair. They discuss why this is important.

indicators.description: Community circle. Children singing 'This is the way I brush my teeth'. They mime the action. Teacher writes 'Brush teeth' on the board.

exemplars.description: Children asking questions about hygiene. One child asks 'Why do we bathe?'. Another answers 'To smell good'. Interactive discussion.

indicators.description: Teacher showing the cover of a book about hygiene. She points to the title and illustration. Children predict what the book is about.

exemplars.description: Children acting out words from a story they just read, like 'washing' and 'combing'. They use props like a sponge and comb.

indicators.description: Children singing rhymes. They emphasize rhyming words at the end of lines (e.g., 'hair' and 'care'). They clap when they hear the rhyme.

exemplars.description: A child pointing to their ear saying 'Hear'. Another points to a picture of a 'Bear'. They laugh at the rhyme. Phonological awareness game.

indicators.description: A name tag game. Name cards are clipped to a line. Children find their own name tag and peg it. They are recognizing their names.

exemplars.description: Children pointing to letters in their names on a wall chart. They spell out their names to a friend. 'K-O-F-I'.

indicators.description: Teacher introducing a tongue twister with a target sound. Children repeat it, trying to say it fast. They identify the sound.

exemplars.description: Children writing a key word (e.g., 'Soap') in their books. They focus on writing legibly. The teacher assists with pencil grip.

indicators.description: Children creating a 'Self-Dictionary'. They draw a toothbrush and write 'Brush' underneath. They color the pictures brightly.

exemplars.description: A child showing their drawing of a towel and soap. They read the labels they wrote. The teacher nods in approval.

indicators.description: Children weighing hygiene items (soap, sponge) on a simple balance scale. They determine which is heavier. Using math vocabulary.

exemplars.description: Children using symbols '<', '>', '=' on cards to compare numbers of hygiene items (e.g., 5 soaps > 2 brushes). Math integration.

subStrands.title: Eating good food and taking my vaccinations to keep my body healthy
subStrands.description: Learners explore healthy food, balanced diet, vaccination, and simple habits for staying healthy.

contentStandards.description: Children discussing a 'Balanced Diet' chart. They point to proteins, carbohydrates, and vitamins. Some hold plastic food items representing the groups.

indicators.description: Community circle discussion. Children talk about foods that make them grow. One child holds a yam, another an egg. They look happy and healthy.

exemplars.description: Children looking at a computer or chart showing a balanced diet. They contribute ideas about what they eat at home. Interactive learning.

indicators.description: Teacher reading a Big Book about diseases. She shows pictures of sick people. Children answer questions about why they got sick (e.g. poor diet).

exemplars.description: Children acting out words from the health story. One pretends to wash hands, another pretends to eat fruit. Understanding through action.

indicators.description: Children clapping syllables of long health words like 'Vac-ci-na-tion'. They count the claps (4). They are stretching words and blending sounds.

exemplars.description: A child saying 'Tu-ber-cu-lo-sis' slowly, counting 5 syllables on their fingers. The teacher smiles. Phonological awareness activity.

indicators.description: Teacher flashing sight word cards (e.g., 'the', 'can', 'is'). Children read them instantly. They use the words to make oral sentences about health.

exemplars.description: Children finding sight words in a text about diseases. They point to 'the' and 'to'. They write a simple sentence in their books.

indicators.description: Children practicing writing a letter sound for the week. They write it in the air, then in their books. The keyword is related to health (e.g., 'F' for Food).

exemplars.description: Learners sitting at desks writing letters and words legibly on blue and red lines. They are focused on handwriting practice.

indicators.description: Children drawing healthy foods in their 'Self-Dictionary'. One draws an orange, another fish. They color them and label them with invented spelling.

exemplars.description: A child copying the names of food items from the board into their book under their drawings. Literacy and art integration.

indicators.description: Children comparing a big yam and a small potato. They say 'The yam is bigger'. They compare a big water bottle and a small one. Measuring size and weight.

exemplars.description: A child holding two fruits, estimating which is heavier. They place them on a balance scale to check. Hands-on math.

subStrands.title: My Environment and My Health
subStrands.description: Learners identify safe and unsafe features in their environment and discuss how the environment affects health.

contentStandards.description: Classroom discussion about a poster on pollution. Children look concerned about dirty water. They suggest cleaning it up. Environmental awareness.

indicators.description: Children walking outside with the teacher. They point to broken glass (unsafe) and a playground swing (safe). They are learning to identify hazards.

exemplars.description: Children discussing cleanliness in a circle. One mimics sweeping. They talk about keeping the environment safe from diseases.

indicators.description: Teacher reading 'Adzoa has Malaria' to the class. Children ask questions about mosquitoes. They discuss using bed nets. Active listening.

exemplars.description: Children identifying the illustrator and author of a book. They look at the back cover. Literacy skills in context.

indicators.description: Children identifying sounds in environment words. 'Sand' starts with /s/ and ends with /d/. They clap syllables for 'Gut-ter'. Phonics practice.

exemplars.description: A child holding a picture of a 'Rat'. They say the beginning sound /r/. Another child holds 'Fly' and says /f/. Phonemic awareness.

indicators.description: Children blending sounds to say 'Cut-lass'. They write the word in their books. Teacher helps with spacing. Literacy and safety vocab.

exemplars.description: Close up of exercise book. Child writing 'Safe' and 'Clean'. Handwriting practice with red and blue lines.

indicators.description: Children drawing dangerous objects like a knife or open socket. They label them 'Danger'. Awareness of safety hazards.

exemplars.description: A child drawing a banana peel on the floor. They explain why it is dangerous (slipping). Visualizing safety.

indicators.description: Household corner. Children sorting objects. Putting 'dangerous' items (plastic knife) in one box and 'safe' items (spoon) in another. Classification.

exemplars.description: Children sorting shapes by color. Red triangles in one group, blue circles in another. Numeracy integration.

subStrands.title: Protecting ourselves from road accidents and harmful strangers
subStrands.description: Learners explore basic personal safety, including road safety and staying safe from harmful strangers.

contentStandards.description: Children discussing 'Strangers'. A teacher explains not to go with unknown people. Children practicing saying 'No!' politely but firmly.

indicators.description: Community circle. Children singing a traffic light song ('Red means Stop'). They act out the lights. A poster shows road safety rules.

exemplars.description: Children role-playing avoiding sharp objects. One child warns another 'Don't touch!'. Safety education.

indicators.description: Shared reading. Teacher reading from left to right. Children following the text. KWL chart about safety on the board.

exemplars.description: Children picking keywords from the text like 'Hurt' and acting them out. One child pretends to have a hurt finger. Comprehension check.

indicators.description: Phonics revision. Teacher shows letter 'H' for 'Harm'. Children write it in the air. They write 'Harm' in their books. Handwriting practice.

exemplars.description: Children writing sentences about safety in exercise books. 'I walk safe'. Focused writing time.

indicators.description: Children think-pair-sharing about what to draw. They draw a scene of running away from a stranger. They color it and explain it.

exemplars.description: A child labeling their drawing 'Stop'. The drawing shows a hand signaling stop to a car. Safety art.

indicators.description: Children sorting objects by color (red items, blue items). They count them. They compare piles using 'more than' cards. Math with objects.

exemplars.description: Children placing a '<' sign between a small pile of sticks and a large pile. They are learning comparison symbols.

strands.title: MY FAMILY
strands.description: Learners explore family types, family history, celebrations, and the rules that guide home and school family life.

subStrands.title: Types and members of my Family
subStrands.description: Learners identify family members and discuss their rights, roles, and responsibilities.

contentStandards.description: Children demonstrating rights and responsibilities. A child reading a book (right to education). Another sweeping (responsibility). Teacher facilitates.

indicators.description: Community circle. Teacher displays an Extended Family poster. Children recite a poem about family. Discussion about family members.

exemplars.description: Children taking turns to name who lives in their house. They count family members on their fingers. Sharing family stories.

indicators.description: Teacher showing a book about families. Scaffolding opening book from left to right. Reading an informational text. KWL chart visible.

exemplars.description: Children sharing what they learnt (L) about family roles. One says 'Dad works'. Another says 'Mom cares'. Teacher writes it down.

indicators.description: Children mentioning names of family members. Teacher lists them. Children clap syllables for 'Fa-ther', 'Mo-ther'. Identifying initial sounds /f/, /m/.

exemplars.description: Children identifying letters associated with family roles. 'F' for Father. They find the letter card. Phonemic awareness.

indicators.description: Teacher revising letter sounds. Children identify sounds in family words. They write the letters in their books.

exemplars.description: Children writing 'Dad' legibly in their books. Teacher checks pencil grip. Writing practice.

indicators.description: Children creating a family tree collage. Cutting and pasting pictures of people on a tree drawing. Writing names next to pictures.

exemplars.description: Warm up exercise tapping fingers. Teacher models writing a letter in the air. Children write the letter in their books. Handwriting prep.

indicators.description: Teacher presenting a word problem using pictures. '3 learners + 2 parents'. Children counting all people to find the sum 5. Addition concept.

exemplars.description: Children doing simple addition sums in books. 2 + 3 = 5. Using counters to help. Transition to abstract addition.

subStrands.title: Origin and Family History
subStrands.description: Learners explore family origin, history, home language, and cultural background.

contentStandards.description: Children listening to a story about where families come from. They are asking questions. Teacher explains migration simply.

indicators.description: Community circle. Singing indigenous songs. Children stating their home language and family name. Discussing origins.

exemplars.description: Children sharing a traditional food item or story from their family history. Class listens respectfully. Cultural appreciation.

indicators.description: Teacher reading 'Family Picture' story. Children identify author/illustrator. Using Herringbone strategy (Who, What, Where chart) to answer questions.

exemplars.description: Children retelling the family history story in their own words. They point to pictures in the book to support their telling.

indicators.description: Children identifying sight words like 'brother', 'sister' in a text. Teacher lists them on board. Flash card reading practice.

exemplars.description: Children writing sight words in their word banks. They read the words to a partner. Building vocabulary.

indicators.description: Children clapping syllables of tribe names (e.g. 'A-kan'). Identifying sounds. Decoding words using letter sounds.

exemplars.description: Children grouping letter cards to form names of tribes. Teacher assists with sounds. Phonological awareness.

indicators.description: Teacher reviewing letter sounds. Children writing letters and keywords in books. Handwriting practice.

exemplars.description: Children writing 'Ga' or 'Ewe' in their books. They ensure letters sit on the line. Writing skills.

indicators.description: Resource person (elder) telling stories of origin. Children listening. Dramatizing the story in costume. Singing songs.

exemplars.description: Children acting out a migration story. They pretend to walk a long journey. They wear traditional cloth. Cultural history.

indicators.description: Children measuring classroom length with feet. Using rope to measure distance to headteacher's office. Comparing lengths 'longer than', 'shorter than'.

exemplars.description: Children using a ruler to measure a table. They record the number. They estimate distance on a map. Measurement activity.

subStrands.title: Family Celebrations and Festivals
subStrands.description: Learners discuss family celebrations, festivals, and the activities associated with them.

contentStandards.description: Children talking about festivals. Display of festival items (drum, food bowl). Singing songs. Understanding importance of celebrations.

indicators.description: Community circle. Poster of celebration. Discussing activities (eating, dancing). Singing folk tunes. Sharing experiences.

exemplars.description: Children dancing to a religious song. They look happy. They mime playing instruments. Celebrating culture.

indicators.description: Teacher showing book cover. Children predict story. Read aloud narrative. Answering 'wh' questions. Using Herringbone chart.

exemplars.description: Children answering questions about the story characters. They explain what happened. Comprehension check.

indicators.description: Reading sight words on flash cards (e.g., 'happy', 'gift'). Children find them in the big book. Copying words into books.

exemplars.description: Children writing 'birthday' in their word bank. They draw a cake next to it. Building vocabulary.

indicators.description: Teacher listing festival names. Children clap syllables. Identify initial letter sounds. Phonological awareness.

exemplars.description: Children clapping 'Christ-mas' (2 claps). Identifying /c/ sound. Sorting words by initial sound.

indicators.description: Revising letter sounds. Writing letter names of festivals in exercise books. Legible writing practice.

exemplars.description: Children sitting at desks writing 'Eid' carefully. Teacher checking work. Handwriting focus.

indicators.description: Children making beads from paper and straws. Rolling paper with glue. Threading beads. Preparing for celebration.

exemplars.description: Children wearing their handmade beads. Role playing a festival procession. Creative arts.

indicators.description: Classroom store. Children using real or play money to buy ingredients for a meal. Counting money and change. Making a shopping list.

exemplars.description: Children solving addition/subtraction word problems about shopping. 'Bought 3 tomatoes, used 1'. Numeracy in context.

subStrands.title: My School Family
subStrands.description: Learners identify members of the school family and discuss the rules that guide life in school.

contentStandards.description: Children discussing school rules. Teacher writing them on board. Children modeling 'walking feet' and 'quiet voices'. Understanding community rules.

indicators.description: Community circle. Discussing posters of classroom and library. Talking about members of school family (Head, teachers). Creating simple rules together.

exemplars.description: Children role-playing being good friends. Sharing a book. Demonstrating rules in action.

indicators.description: Predicting a story from book cover. Reading aloud narrative. Answering 'wh' questions using Herringbone strategy. Literacy focus.

exemplars.description: Children confirming their predictions after reading. Discussing the problem and solution in the story.

indicators.description: Children reading new vocabulary on word cards. Practicing pronunciation. Using words to make simple sentences about school rules.

exemplars.description: A child saying a sentence 'I share my toys'. Teacher writes it. Vocabulary application.

indicators.description: Teacher revising letter sounds. Children writing letter in air, on arms, then in books. Focus on legibility.

exemplars.description: Children practicing writing a letter on a slate. They check each other's work.

indicators.description: Children drawing objects that communicate rules (bell, drum). Tracing and coloring. Labeling the object. Art and literacy.

exemplars.description: A child showing a drawing of a school bell. They explain what it means (time for class). Teacher affirms.

indicators.description: Children measuring classroom items with feet/rope. Comparing lengths 'longer than', 'shorter than'. Comparing heights of learners back-to-back.

exemplars.description: Two children standing back-to-back. Another child decides who is taller. Practical measurement activity.

strands.title: VALUES AND BELIEFS
strands.description: Learners develop personal, cultural, national, civic, and religious values, and learn to relate well with people of different beliefs.

subStrands.title: My Personal Values
subStrands.description: Learners discuss personal likes, dislikes, and values that influence how they live with others.

contentStandards.description: Children in a circle discussing values. The teacher writes 'Good Manners' on the board. Children demonstrate sharing toys. Positive behavior focus.

indicators.description: Community Circle time. Children face each other in pairs. One speaks while the other listens. They are discussing what they like about their friends. Respectful communication.

exemplars.description: Children role-playing a conversation about likes and dislikes. One holds a red card (dislike) and explains why they don't like fighting. Another holds a green card (like) for sharing.

indicators.description: Teacher showing the cover of 'The Cat's Hat' (or similar story). She points to the title. Children raise hands to predict the story based on the illustration.

exemplars.description: Children filling in a 'Herringbone' graphic organizer on the floor with word cards (Who, What, Where). They are discussing a story they heard. Comprehension activity.

indicators.description: A phonics game. Teacher makes a letter sound. Children run to pick up the corresponding letter card from a table. They clap the syllables of a word starting with that letter.

exemplars.description: Children listening to the word 'Table'. They identify the beginning letter 'T'. Then they clap twice for 'Ta-ble'. Active listening.

indicators.description: Children identifying key words on flash cards (e.g. 'Love', 'Share'). They copy the words into their 'Self-Dictionary' books and draw a picture next to it.

exemplars.description: Close-up of a child's journal. They have written the word 'Play' and drawn two stick figures playing ball. Literacy and art integration.

subStrands.title: My Cultural Values
subStrands.description: Learners explore culturally valued virtues, manners, greetings, and behaviour patterns.

contentStandards.description: Classroom display of cultural virtues. Children act out being polite—giving items with the right hand. The teacher smiles approvingly.

indicators.description: Community circle. Children taking turns to demonstrate a greeting with appropriate facial expressions (smiling, making eye contact). Conversational poster on Greetings is visible.

exemplars.description: A child pretending to be an elder sitting in a chair. Another child approaches, lowers their height slightly, and greets 'Good morning'. Cultural role-play.

indicators.description: Children using a 'Story Map' graphic organizer. They draw the setting and characters of a story about respect. They are retelling the story to a partner.

exemplars.description: Teacher reading aloud. She pauses to ask 'What is the problem in the story?'. Children look thoughtful. They identify that the character was rude.

indicators.description: A lively phonics game. Children moving around. Teacher calls a letter sound. Children find an object or word card in the room that starts with that sound.

exemplars.description: Children picking a letter card 'M'. They say 'M is for Manners'. They clap the syllables of 'Man-ners'. Interactive learning.

indicators.description: Children copying daily greetings like 'Good Morning', 'Good Afternoon' into their note books. They are checking the board for spelling. Writing practice.

exemplars.description: Pairs of learners reading greetings to each other from their self-dictionaries. One reads, the other responds with the appropriate gesture.

subStrands.title: My National and Civic Values
subStrands.description: Learners identify values and behaviours expected of good Ghanaian learners and citizens.

contentStandards.description: Children brainstorming 'Good Ghanaian Behaviours'. Teacher writes 'Truth', 'Obedience' on the board. Children give thumbs up to pictures of good behaviour.

indicators.description: Community Circle. Children discussing a poster showing hospitality (offering water). They volunteer to act out a scene of welcoming a visitor. Civic values.

exemplars.description: A skit in the classroom. A child knocks on a pretend door. Another opens it and offers a seat warmly. The class claps. Learning hospitality.

indicators.description: Teacher reading a narrative about Kwame Nkrumah or a national hero. Children listening. They use a Story Map to recall who the hero was and what they did.

exemplars.description: Children drawing a picture of a national hero based on the story read. They attempt to write the hero's name under the drawing.

indicators.description: Children creating a short drama about 'Truthfulness'. One child admits to breaking a toy, and the 'teacher' forgives them. Demonstrating honesty.

exemplars.description: Children acting out a scene where a police officer catches a thief. They use vocabulary like 'Stop', 'Law', 'Good citizen'. Patriotic drama.

indicators.description: Teacher reviewing a letter sound (e.g., 'P' for Patriotism/Police). Children write the letter 'P' in the air and then in their books.

exemplars.description: Children writing the word 'Ghana' in their books. They focus on the capital 'G'. They color the word in red, yellow, and green.

subStrands.title: Our Beliefs
subStrands.description: Learners learn to relate well with people of different beliefs, cultures, and languages.

contentStandards.description: Children engaging in a sorting activity. They group pictures of people by clothing/culture, then mix them up to show everyone playing together. Promoting tolerance.

indicators.description: Community Circle. Children discussing a poster of diverse people. Teacher prompts 'How do we treat everyone?'. Children answer 'With love'.

exemplars.description: A game where children find a partner who speaks a different language or is from a different tribe. They shake hands and smile. Celebrating diversity.

indicators.description: Picture walk through a Big Book about a religious story (e.g., David and Goliath). Children predict the ending. They use a Story Map to analyze characters.

exemplars.description: Children drawing 'David' and 'Goliath'. They compare the sizes (small and big). They write 'David' under the small boy. Literacy integration.

indicators.description: Teacher displaying sight word cards from the religious story. Children read them aloud. They find the words in the Big Book text.

exemplars.description: Children forming sentences with sight word cards on their tables. 'God is good'. They copy the sentence into their books.

indicators.description: A 'Letter Ladder' game drawn on the floor. A grid with letters. Children hop onto the letter that matches the sound the teacher calls out.

exemplars.description: Children playing in teams. Teacher says a word from the story. First child to jump on the beginning letter wins. Active phonics.

strands.title: MY LOCAL COMMUNITY
strands.description: Learners identify special places, occupations, and leaders in their local community and understand their roles.

subStrands.title: Knowing the Special Places in My Community
subStrands.description: Learners identify special places in the local community and discuss what happens there.

contentStandards.description: Community circle. A large poster of a village/town layout. Children identify the market and the school. They share stories of visiting these places.

indicators.description: Children sitting on mats, looking at pictures of special places. One child holds a picture of a Chief's Palace and describes what happens there.

exemplars.description: A field trip scene. Children observing a police station. They see a police officer in uniform. They look excited and curious.

indicators.description: Teacher reading an informational text about 'My Community'. She uses a KWL chart. Children participate by asking questions about the places mentioned.

exemplars.description: Children raising hands to answer questions about the read-aloud. 'Where do we buy food?'. They answer 'Market'. Teacher points to the word 'Market' in the book.

indicators.description: Reading sight words from the big book. Words like 'School', 'Shop', 'Clinic' are on flashcards. Children match cards to pictures in the book.

exemplars.description: Children writing the word 'School' in their notebooks. They draw a picture of their school next to it. Vocabulary building.

indicators.description: An 'Alphabet Relay' game. Two teams of children. They run to the board to write a letter called out by the teacher. Fun and competitive.

exemplars.description: Children writing capital and small letters on the board (e.g., Mm). Their teammates cheer. Letter recognition practice.

indicators.description: Teacher introducing the letter 'M' for Market. Children write 'M' in the air. They write 'Market' in their books, focusing on neatness.

exemplars.description: Children finding words starting with 'M' on a community map poster. They point to 'Mosque' and 'Market'. Phonemic awareness.

subStrands.title: Knowing the Important People / Occupation in My Community
subStrands.description: Learners identify important people and occupations in the community and discuss their work.

contentStandards.description: Community circle. A poster shows various occupations. Children discuss what their parents do. They mime actions of different jobs.

indicators.description: Discussion about neighbors' jobs. Children hold up pictures of a baker, a driver, and a fisher. They talk about why these jobs are important.

exemplars.description: Children stating which job they like. 'I want to be a nurse'. They stand in groups based on their choice.

indicators.description: Teacher reading a Big Book about 'The Baker'. Children track the words. They use a KWL chart to record facts about baking.

exemplars.description: Children sharing lessons learnt (L). One says 'The baker makes bread'. They draw a baker and write a simple sentence.

indicators.description: Children giving an oral composition. A child in a police uniform stands in front of the class and says 'I am a police officer. I catch thieves'.

exemplars.description: Children writing simple sentences in their word bank. 'I am a teacher'. 'I help people'. Using new vocabulary.

indicators.description: Teacher revising letter sounds. Children write the letter 'N' for Nurse. They practice writing 'Nurse' on the lines in their books.

exemplars.description: Children identifying the sound /d/ in Doctor and Driver. They circle the letter 'D' on a worksheet.

subStrands.title: Knowing the Special Leaders in Our Community and Country
subStrands.description: Learners identify community and national leaders and discuss their roles.

contentStandards.description: Children role-playing a meeting of leaders. One acts as the Chief, listening to people. They learn about solving problems.

indicators.description: Community circle. Talking about the roles of political (Assemblyman), traditional (Chief), and religious leaders. A poster shows them working together.

exemplars.description: Children matching picture cards of leaders to their symbols (e.g., Chief - Stool, Pastor - Bible). Understanding symbols of authority.

indicators.description: Teacher reading 'The Chief' Big Book. Children tracking words. They use KWL chart to discuss what chiefs do (settle disputes, celebrate festivals).

exemplars.description: Children answering questions about the Queen Mother from the story. They share what they learnt about her role.

indicators.description: Children identifying keywords like 'Durbar', 'Stool', 'Staff'. They use them to make oral sentences. 'The Chief sits on a stool'.

exemplars.description: Children dramatizing a leader's role using the keywords. A 'Chief' holds a 'Staff' and speaks to the people.

indicators.description: A blending game. Teacher writes letters on the board. Points to them slowly to blend sounds into a word like 'Mat'. Children repeat.

exemplars.description: Two children holding letter cards standing next to each other. They move closer to blend the sounds into a word. Physical phonics.

strands.title: MY NATION GHANA
strands.description: Learners explore Ghana’s history, identity, symbols, and national celebrations.

subStrands.title: History and Celebrations of Ghana
subStrands.description: Learners explore Ghana’s history, independence, and national celebrations.

contentStandards.description: A classroom drama. Children dressed as historical figures (e.g., Kwame Nkrumah) wearing traditional cloth. They are reenacting the independence declaration. Other children clap.

indicators.description: Community Circle time. Teacher telling the story of 6th March. Children act out marching. A child holds a flag. Discussing freedom.

exemplars.description: Children listening to a resource person (an elder) telling a story about Ghana's past. They sit on mats attentively. They raise hands to share what they learnt (L).

indicators.description: Shared reading of a book about Independence Day. Teacher reads with expression. Children interrupt politely to ask 'Why are they happy?'. KWL chart on board.

exemplars.description: Children looking at pictures in a history book. They discuss the clothing people wore long ago. Teacher guides the conversation using the KWL chart.

indicators.description: Children using word cards related to independence (e.g., 'Flag', 'March', 'Free'). They arrange them to make a simple sentence: 'We march today'. Writing practice.

exemplars.description: Children dramatizing a march past. One acts as a commander shouting 'Left, Right'. Others follow instructions. Learning action words.

indicators.description: Rhyming game. Teacher says 'Cap'. Children suggest 'Map', 'Tap'. They clap when words rhyme. Replacing sounds to make new words.

exemplars.description: Children playing with letter cards. They change the first letter of 'Day' to 'Say' and 'Pay'. Visual phonics activity.

indicators.description: Letter Ladder game floor mat. A grid with letters drawn on the floor. Children hop onto the letter that corresponds to a spoken word's start sound. Active learning.

exemplars.description: Children in teams playing 'Letter Hop'. A child jumps on 'G' when the teacher says 'Ghana'. The class cheers.

strands.title: ALL AROUND US
strands.description: Learners explore living and non-living things, animals, water, air, plants, soil, gardening, light, and changing weather conditions.

subStrands.title: Living and Non-Living Things
subStrands.description: Learners distinguish between living and non-living things in their environment.

contentStandards.description: Nature walk. Teacher and students walking in the school garden. They point to a bird flying (living) and a wall (non-living). Observation skills.

indicators.description: Community Circle. Displaying real objects: a stone and a potted plant. Children debating which one needs water. Classification discussion.

exemplars.description: Children returning from a nature walk with collected items. They place leaves in one basket and pebbles in another. Discussing what they saw.

indicators.description: Shared reading of a book about 'Living Things'. Children gathered around the teacher. Teacher asks 'Is a car living?'. Children shout 'No!'. Interactive reading.

exemplars.description: KWL chart on board about Nature. Children share what they learnt (L) from the story. Teacher writes 'Plants grow'.

indicators.description: Children writing new words like 'Tree', 'Bird', 'Stone' in their notebooks. They look at word cards for spelling help. Vocabulary focus.

exemplars.description: Teacher writing 'Living' and 'Non-living' on the board. Children copy the words and draw one example under each heading.

indicators.description: Alphabet Relay game outdoors. Two teams running to the chalkboard to write a letter called out by the teacher. High energy literacy game.

exemplars.description: Children celebrating after writing the correct letter 'B' on the board during a relay game. Teamwork and letter recognition.

indicators.description: Phonics review. Teacher showing a letter card 'S'. Children look for objects starting with 'S' (sand, stone, stick). They write 'S' in the air.

exemplars.description: Children writing the word 'Sun' in their books. They draw a sun next to it. Focusing on the initial 'S' sound.

subStrands.title: Living Things - Domestic and Wild Animals
subStrands.description: Learners identify domestic and wild animals and discuss their importance.

contentStandards.description: Children role-playing animal care. One child 'feeds' a toy dog. Another 'builds' a coop for chickens with blocks. Emphasizing care for domestic animals.

indicators.description: Community Circle. Discussing animals at home vs in the bush. Children mimic animal sounds. 'Roar' for lion, 'Meow' for cat.

exemplars.description: Children holding up pictures of animals. They stand in two groups: 'Home' and 'Bush'. They talk about what the animals eat.

indicators.description: Shared reading of a folktale about animals (e.g., Why the dog lives with man). Children listening intently. Predicting what happens next.

exemplars.description: Children using a Story Map to draw the characters (dog, man) and the setting (forest, house) of the folktale. Comprehension check.

indicators.description: LEA session. Teacher writing 'Animals help us' on chart paper. Children dictating sentences about what animals do. 'Dogs guard the house'.

exemplars.description: Children illustrating the class story about animals. They draw a dog barking at a stranger. They write 'Dog' under the picture.

indicators.description: Children singing 'Old MacDonald'. They clap for each syllable of the animals mentioned: 'Cow' (1 clap), 'Chi-cken' (2 claps). Musical literacy.

exemplars.description: Children counting claps for animal names. They hold up fingers to show how many syllables. 'El-e-phant' has 3 syllables.

indicators.description: Teacher showing letter 'C'. Children say 'Cat'. Teacher showing 'D'. Children say 'Dog'. Revision of initial sounds.

exemplars.description: Pupils blending sounds. Two children stand together holding 'C', 'a', 't'. They move closer to blend 'Cat'. Active spelling.

subStrands.title: Water
subStrands.description: Learners explore sources, importance, uses, and care of water.

contentStandards.description: Children demonstrating water uses. One pretends to drink, another pretends to wash clothes. They look at a poster showing plants needing water.

indicators.description: Community Circle. Discussing sources of water (tap, well, rain). Reciting a poem about rain. Teacher writes sources on the board.

exemplars.description: Children watching a video or looking at a poster about water. They dictate a story to the teacher about 'How we use water at home'. LEA session.

indicators.description: Shared reading of 'The Thirsty Crow'. Children looking at pictures. Teacher asks 'Why did the crow need water?'. Inferential thinking.

exemplars.description: Children brainstorming why water is important after the story. They answer story map questions about the crow. Teacher writes answers.

indicators.description: Children creating a text about water using LEA. They say sentences like 'Water helps plants grow'. Teacher writes it clearly. Children read it back.

exemplars.description: Children illustrating their class story about water. Drawing flowers growing with rain. They label 'Rain' and 'Flower'.

indicators.description: Phonics blending. Teacher writes 'T', 'a', 'p'. Children sound out /t/ /a/ /p/ -> Tap. They write 'Tap' in their books.

exemplars.description: Children working in pairs. One holds letter cards, the other blends them to say the word (e.g. Pot, Cup). Fun reading practice.

subStrands.title: Air
subStrands.description: Learners explore air as an important natural resource all around us.

contentStandards.description: Teacher explaining air helps living things. Children taking deep breaths. They point to a plant swaying in the wind. Understanding invisible resources.

indicators.description: Community circle. Discussing the importance of air. Teacher shows a deflated ball and an inflated one. Children talk about the difference.

exemplars.description: Nature walk. Children observing leaves moving. They share their experiences 'The wind is blowing'. Experiential learning.

indicators.description: LEA activity. Children observing a fan. They dictate sentences: 'The fan gives us air'. Teacher scribes. They read it together.

exemplars.description: Children drawing a picture to go with their air story. Drawing a kite flying. They write 'Kite' next to it.

indicators.description: Read aloud about Air. KWL strategy. Children identify spaces between words in a sentence on the board. 'Air is good'.

exemplars.description: Children pointing to spaces between words in a big book with a pointer. Visualizing text structure.

indicators.description: Practice Ladder game drawn on floor. Grid has sight words like 'Is', 'It', 'The'. Children jump on the word the teacher reads. Active reading.

exemplars.description: Children cheering as a friend lands on the correct sight word. Happy, competitive learning game.

indicators.description: Pupils blending process. Children holding cards 'F', 'a', 'n'. They blend to say 'Fan'. They write 'Fan' in exercise books.

exemplars.description: Teacher checking children's writing. They are writing 'Fan' and 'Man'. Focusing on correct letter formation.

subStrands.title: Plants - 1
subStrands.description: Learners identify parts of plants and discuss their uses.

contentStandards.description: Children in the classroom painting pictures of plants. They are labeling the parts. A display table has real fruits and vegetables (food from plants). Understanding plant benefits.

indicators.description: Community circle. Teacher holding a real plant (uprooted to show roots). Children discuss the parts. A poster shows a diagram of a maize plant.

exemplars.description: Children observing a conversational poster of plants. They take turns pointing to parts that make food (leaves) and parts that hold the plant (roots).

indicators.description: Language Experience Approach (LEA). Children dictating sentences about plants to the teacher. 'Roots go down'. Teacher writes on large paper. Collaborative writing.

exemplars.description: Children reading the class-created text about plants together. One child uses a pointer to track the words. The text has small drawings next to keywords.

indicators.description: Teacher reading aloud the LEA text. Children listening and raising hands to share 'L' (what they learnt) for the KWL chart. Reflective learning.

exemplars.description: Children participating in a Q&A about the plant text. Teacher points to the word 'Leaf'. A child explains its use.

indicators.description: Practice Ladder game with sight words. A ladder drawn on the ground. Rungs have words like 'Tree', 'Leaf', 'Root'. Children hop on the words they can read.

exemplars.description: Children cheering as a friend successfully reads a sight word on the ladder. Active literacy game.

indicators.description: Teacher revising letter sounds. Children blending sounds to make two-syllable words. 'Gar-den'. They write the word in their books.

exemplars.description: Children sitting in pairs helping each other blend words. One holds 'Flow', the other 'er'. They say 'Flower'. Peer learning.

subStrands.title: Plants - 2
subStrands.description: Learners explore what plants need to grow and how plants grow.

contentStandards.description: Classroom experiment. Two plants, one covered with a box (no light), one in the sun. Children comparing them. Discussing needs like light and water.

indicators.description: Community circle. Discussing nutrients. Teacher shows soil and water. Children sing 'Plants need water'. Interactive discussion.

exemplars.description: Nature walk. Children looking for healthy and unhealthy plants. They point to a dried leaf. They discuss why it dried up (no water).

indicators.description: LEA activity. Children observing their bean plant experiment. Dictating: 'The bean grew big'. Teacher writes on chart.

exemplars.description: Children copying the LEA story into their books. They draw a picture of their bean plant next to the text.

indicators.description: Teacher reading a Big Book about a farmer. Children participate by making digging actions. They answer questions about what the farmer did first.

exemplars.description: Children sharing lessons learnt from the story. One says 'Plants need sun'. Teacher adds this to the KWL chart.

indicators.description: Blending activity. Children blending sounds to make words like 'Seed', 'Grow'. Writing the words boldly on lines.

exemplars.description: Teacher conducting a 'Pupils blending process'. A child comes to the front to blend sounds on the board. Others watch and clap.

subStrands.title: Types of Soil and Gardening
subStrands.description: Learners identify types of soil and explore gardening activities.

contentStandards.description: Garden area. Children trying to plant in hard clay versus soft loam. Discussing which is easier. Hands-on science.

indicators.description: Community circle. Reciting a poem about soil. Discussing which soil is best for gardening. Teacher writes 'Loam' on board.

exemplars.description: Children observing a poster showing crops growing in good soil. They identify the crops (maize, tomato). Interactive discussion.

indicators.description: Read aloud of informational text about soil. Teacher asks inferential questions 'Why did the plant die?'. Children answer.

exemplars.description: Children arranging cut-up sentences about soil. They count the words. 'Soil helps plants'. Literacy and numeracy.

indicators.description: LEA session. Children dictating 'Clay is sticky'. Teacher writes it. Children read it back. Creating reading material.

exemplars.description: Children copying the sentence 'Loam is good' into books. They draw a pot with a plant. Writing practice.

indicators.description: Phoneme substitution game. Teacher says 'Pot'. Children change /p/ to /h/ to make 'Hot'. They laugh and try other words.

exemplars.description: Children adding new words to the Word Wall. 'Dig', 'Pig', 'Big'. Recognizing rhyming patterns and initial sounds.

subStrands.title: Natural and Man-Made (Artificial) Sources of Light
subStrands.description: Learners identify natural and artificial sources of light and discuss their usefulness.

contentStandards.description: Children sorting pictures of light sources. Sun and firefly (Natural). Torch and candle (Man-made). Discussing usefulness.

indicators.description: Community circle. Reciting 'Twinkle Twinkle'. Discussing what gives light. Teacher shows a real torch and candle.

exemplars.description: Children classifying light sources on a chart. Placing stickers under 'Natural' or 'Artificial'. Critical thinking.

indicators.description: Read aloud about 'Lights at Night'. Children counting words in a sentence from the book. Discussing how streetlights help us.

exemplars.description: Children answering questions about the story. 'What happened when the lights went out?'. They relate it to their own experiences.

indicators.description: LEA session. Children dictating 'The sun gives us light'. Teacher writes. Children read along.

exemplars.description: Children copying the LEA text into their books. They draw a big sun. Integrating writing and art.

indicators.description: Letter Bingo game. Children have cards with letters. Teacher calls a sound. Children tick the letter. Fun assessment.

exemplars.description: Children shouting 'Bingo!' when they tick all letters. Identifying letter sounds in names of environment items.

indicators.description: Children using letter cards to form words like 'Sun', 'Lamp'. They match the word to a picture. Word building.

exemplars.description: Group work. Children forming simple sight words 'is', 'it', 'on'. Teacher checks spelling.

subStrands.title: Changing Weather Conditions
subStrands.description: Learners identify changing weather conditions and discuss their effects.

contentStandards.description: Children discussing effects of weather. Poster shows flooding (negative) and drying clothes (positive). They talk about staying safe.

indicators.description: Community circle. Reciting a weather rhyme. Describing the current weather. 'It is sunny'. Teacher points to the sun symbol.

exemplars.description: Children drawing the weather for the day. Sun and clouds. They share their drawings.

indicators.description: Shared reading of a weather story. Children answering simple questions. 'What did the wind do?'. Comprehension.

exemplars.description: KWL strategy. Children sharing experiences of a big rainstorm. Teacher writes notes.

indicators.description: LEA session. Creating a text 'The rain is wet'. Children dictating. Teacher scribing.

exemplars.description: Children reading the class weather story. They point to words they know. Literacy confidence.

indicators.description: Teacher showing sight words 'Hot', 'Cold', 'Wet'. Children read them. They form sentences 'The sun is hot'.

exemplars.description: Children copying weather sentences into their books. They draw appropriate pictures.

indicators.description: Children identifying letters in names of people from other countries (e.g., 'Kofi' vs 'Pierre'). Recognizing diversity in names.

exemplars.description: A game finding name cards. Children match names to flags. 'Ama' - Ghana, 'John' - UK. Letter recognition.

strands.title: MY GLOBAL COMMUNITY
strands.description: Learners explore transportation, communication, and global connection as ways of relating with the wider world.

subStrands.title: Connecting and Communicating with the Global Community
subStrands.description: Learners explore ways people connect and communicate with the wider world.

contentStandards.description: Children engaging in global connection activities. Identifying transport (ship, plane) on a map. Discussing trade (cocoa leaving Ghana).

indicators.description: Community circle. Reciting a poem about the world. Passing a globe around. Discussing how we visit other countries.

exemplars.description: Children discussing modes of transport. 'Plane goes in air'. 'Ship goes on water'. Holding toy vehicles.

indicators.description: Shared reading of a book about travel. KWL strategy. 'What do you know about planes?'. Children answering questions.

exemplars.description: Children asking questions about the story. 'Where is the ship going?'. Sharing what they learnt.

indicators.description: LEA session on 'Ways we communicate'. Children dictating 'We use phones'. Teacher scribes. Creating a class text.

exemplars.description: Children reading the LEA text together. They circle the word 'Phone'. Literacy practice.

indicators.description: Alphabet Relay. Teams writing letters called by teacher. 'Write the sound /b/'. Children running to board.

exemplars.description: Children cheering as team members write letters correctly. Energetic learning.

indicators.description: Using flash cards to identify key words like 'Ship', 'Bus'. Children writing the words in their books. Dictation practice.

exemplars.description: Children writing the word 'Plane' legibly. Drawing a plane next to it.

indicators.description: Children singing a simple French song (e.g., 'Frère Jacques'). They perform actions. Introduction to foreign language.

exemplars.description: Children learning names of days in French or another language. 'Lundi', 'Mardi'. They clap the rhythm.
